items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: She was good too. It’s Herb’s wife.

ctx.x: You did reference your group with Mel Lewis. I‟m looking at a record date in May, Jazz for Five. That was the first time I saw Wilfred Middlebrooks listed as – credited on a session. So, could you talk about him? You just mentioned that he was the only bassist that would come out for after hours.

He didn‟t partake of the recording scene. The first time I met him was when we were looking for a player. But he was a good player. He should have been doing some other things. He later went with Ella Fitzgerald. Was with her for a long time. Later, Jimmy Rowles had to bow out, because he couldn‟t put up with the late night things, the sessions. So Lorraine Geller came on as the piano player. She was good too. It‟s Herb‟s wife.
Some of the other – as I mentioned earlier, some of the folks who didn‟t have as strong a reputation: drummer Irv Cotler. I saw him listed on a few dates. Any recollections?
